concepts.title: Guitar Orientation
concepts.summary: Identify the body, neck, bridge, strings, frets, and safe playing position.

concepts.title: Standard Tuning
concepts.summary: Recognize the six open strings in standard E-A-D-G-B-E tuning.

concepts.title: Fretting-Hand Shape
concepts.summary: Place the fretting hand with relaxed thumb support and curved fingers.

concepts.title: Pick or Finger Attack
concepts.summary: Produce a controlled single-string attack with a pick or fingertip.

concepts.title: Single-Note Fretting
concepts.summary: Play clean notes while coordinating string selection and fret placement.

concepts.title: Alternate Picking
concepts.summary: Alternate pick direction while keeping repeated notes rhythmically even.

concepts.title: Open Chords
concepts.summary: Form a small set of common open-position major and minor chords.

concepts.title: Basic Strumming
concepts.summary: Strum a chord pattern with a steady pulse and consistent attack.

concepts.title: Chord Changes
concepts.summary: Move between familiar open chords without losing the beat.

concepts.title: Simple Guitar Riff
concepts.summary: Perform a short riff by combining single notes, timing, and controlled attack.

edges.rationale: String identity depends on knowing the instrument layout.
The learner must identify the sounding string.
Clean fretted notes require a stable hand shape.
A note needs a controlled plucking action.
Alternate picking extends controlled single-note attack.
Open chords require relaxed curved fretting fingers.
Strumming is a repeated controlled attack.
Transitions require the chord shapes to be known.
The learner must keep the strumming pulse during a change.
The riff uses repeated single-note attacks.
The final exercise combines the instrument's foundational coordination.
